title_en: The Completed Qur’an Recitation on Behalf of the Deceased
body_ar: هل تجوز الختمة للميت أم لا و هي التي تسمى بالسلكة؟ إن وصول ثواب القرءان للميت بعد موته محل خلاف بين أهل العلم فمذهب مالك والشافعي أنه لا يصل وذالك أن الأصل قول الله تعالى ﴿أم لم ينبأ بما في صحف موسى وإبراهيم الذي وفى أن لا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى وأن سعيه سوف يرى ثم يجزاه الجزاء الأوفى﴾ فعلى هذا الأصل لا يصل هذا العمل بعد الموت أما أبو حنيفة وأحمد فذهبا إلى وصوله قياسا لقراءة القرءان على الصدقة و الحج و العمرة وغير ذالك من أنواع القرب وقد اتفق على أن الصدقة و الدعاء يصلان قطعا وما عداهما كله داخل في الخلاف لأن الصدقة والدعاء ثبت فيهما الأحاديث الصحيحة عن النبي صلى الله عليه و سلم وكذالك الحج و العمرة ثبت فيهما الأحاديث الصحيحة أما ما سوى ذالك كله فلم يرد فيه نص عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ويبقي الخلاف هل هذا من المقدرات التي لا يدخلها القياس أو ليس من المقدرات فيمكن القياس فيه هذا محل خلاف أصولي لا يمكن حسمه و على هذا فالذين يفعلون الختمة عن دبر الميت ويريدون إيصالها إليه فالأحوط بهم والأفضل لهم أن يتصدقوا عنه و أن يدعوا له فهذا الذي يصل بلا خلاف.
body_en:
Question: Is the completed recitation of the Qur’an (khatmah) for the deceased permissible or not — the one that is called al-salkah?

Answer: Whether the reward of the Qur’an reaches the deceased after his death is a point of disagreement among the people of knowledge. The school of Malik and of al-Shafi’i is that it does not reach [him], on the ground that the governing principle is the words of God, be He exalted: {Or has he not been informed of what is in the scriptures of Moses, and of Abraham who fulfilled [his covenant] — that no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another, and that man shall have nothing but what he strove for, and that his striving shall be seen, and then he shall be repaid for it with the fullest repayment} (Sūrat al-Najm 53:36–41). On this principle, this act does not reach [him] after death.

As for Abu Hanifa and Ahmad, they held that it does reach [him], by analogy (qiyās) of the recitation of the Qur’an upon voluntary charity (ṣadaqah), the hajj, the lesser pilgrimage (ʿumrah) and other kinds of pious act. It is agreed that voluntary charity and supplication reach [the deceased] definitively, and everything apart from those two falls within the disagreement — because for voluntary charity and supplication, sound hadiths from the Prophet (may God bless him and grant him peace) are established; and likewise for the hajj and the lesser pilgrimage, sound hadiths are established. As for everything else, no explicit text (naṣṣ) from the Prophet (may God bless him and grant him peace) has come concerning it. And the disagreement remains: is this among the fixed quantities (al-muqaddarāt) into which analogy does not enter, or is it not among the fixed quantities, so that analogy is possible in it? This is a point of disagreement in legal theory (uṣūl) which cannot be settled.

On this basis, those who perform the completed recitation following a person’s death and wish to convey it to him — the more cautious and the better course for them is to give voluntary charity on his behalf and to supplicate for him, for this is what reaches [him] without any disagreement. [Translator's note: renderings of Qur'anic verses here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.]

flags.arabic: الختمة ... و هي التي تسمى بالسلكة
flags.context: هل تجوز الختمة للميت أم لا و هي التي تسمى بالسلكة؟
options: the group Qur’an reading held for the deceased
flags.note: "Al-salkah" is a Mauritanian (Hassaniya) term for the communal khatmah — a gathering at which the Qur’an is recited to completion, here on behalf of a deceased person. The precise form the Sheikh has in view (whether a single sitting, a division of the Qur’an among the attendees, or a recitation over several days) is not specified in the text, and the choice of English affects how readers outside Mauritania will picture the practice. The Sheikh’s office should confirm before a fixed rendering is adopted.
